MOLECULAR GENETICS LABORATORY REPORT
[redacted location] Children's Hospital
Department of Clinical Genetics

PATIENT INFORMATION
Patient Name: [redacted name]
Date of Birth: [redacted date]
Medical Record Number: [redacted ID]
Specimen Type: Whole blood
Date Collected: [redacted date]
Date Received: [redacted date]
Date Reported: [redacted date]

CLINICAL INFORMATION
Referral Reason: Infant testing for suspected Down syndrome
Clinical Features: Clinical features suggestive of trisomy 21

TEST PERFORMED
Quantitative Fluorescence Polymerase Chain Reaction (QF-PCR)
Rapid aneuploidy screening for chromosomes 13, 18, and 21

METHODOLOGY
DNA was extracted from whole blood using standard protocols. QF-PCR analysis was performed using fluorescently labeled primers for chromosome-specific short tandem repeat (STR) markers. The following markers were analyzed:

Chromosome 21: D21S11 (21q21.1), D21S1409 (21q21.2), D21S1435 (21q21.3), D21S1411 (21q22.3)
Chromosome 18: D18S51, D18S386, D18S535, D18S391
Chromosome 13: D13S317, D13S628, D13S634, D13S742

PCR products were analyzed by capillary electrophoresis on an ABI 3500 Genetic Analyzer. Peak areas were calculated and dosage ratios determined for informative markers.

RESULTS

CHROMOSOME 21: ABNORMAL - TRISOMY 21 DETECTED

Marker		Location	Alleles		Peak Ratio	Interpretation
D21S11		21q21.1		3 peaks		1:1:1		Triallelic pattern
D21S1409	21q21.2		2 peaks		2:1		Diallelic pattern (2:1 ratio)
D21S1435	21q21.3		2 peaks		2:1		Diallelic pattern (2:1 ratio)
D21S1411	21q22.3		3 peaks		1:1:1		Triallelic pattern

Four informative markers demonstrate patterns consistent with trisomy 21.

CHROMOSOME 18: NORMAL
All markers show normal biallelic patterns with 1:1 peak ratios

CHROMOSOME 13: NORMAL
All markers show normal biallelic patterns with 1:1 peak ratios

INTERPRETATION
QF-PCR analysis demonstrates trisomy 21 with four informative markers showing either triallelic patterns or diallelic patterns with 2:1 dosage ratios. Chromosomes 13 and 18 show normal complement. These results confirm trisomy 21 indicative of Down syndrome, consistent with the clinical referral indication.

LIMITATIONS
QF-PCR detects only numerical abnormalities of chromosomes 13, 18, and 21. This test does not detect:
- Structural chromosomal abnormalities
- Mosaicism below 20%
- Abnormalities of other chromosomes
- Balanced translocations

RECOMMENDATIONS
Full karyotype analysis of G-banded chromosomes from cultured blood lymphocytes is recommended to:
1. Confirm the QF-PCR findings
2. Determine if trisomy 21 is due to standard trisomy, Robertsonian translocation, or other structural rearrangement
3. Provide accurate genetic counseling regarding recurrence risk

Reported by: [redacted name], PhD, FACMG
Laboratory Director: [redacted name], MD, PhD
